verdict: Reddit's first quarter as a public company grew revenue 48% to $243M and turned adjusted EBITDA positive, but a $596M one-off stock-compensation charge from IPO share vesting drove a $575M GAAP net loss.

kpis.label: Net loss
kpis.note: driven by $596M of stock compensation and related taxes from IPO vesting

kpis.label: Adjusted EBITDA
kpis.note: first positive Q1 — vs -$50.2M a year ago

segments.name: Advertising
segments.note: Ads shown across Reddit's communities — still more than nine dollars in every ten of revenue.

segments.name: Other revenue
segments.note: Data licensing — including AI training deals — plus Reddit Premium subscriptions; up more than fivefold as licensing deals kicked in.

opex.name: Research & development
opex.note: Engineering — swollen this quarter by the one-off stock-compensation charge booked when IPO restricted stock units vested.

opex.name: Sales & marketing
opex.note: The ad sales team and marketing — also carrying a share of the IPO stock-compensation charge.

opex.name: General & administrative
opex.note: Running the company — finance, legal and the back office, plus its share of the IPO stock charge.

otherDetail: Other income of $14.6M, net — $15.4M of interest income, net, earned on Reddit's $1,670.4M of cash and marketable securities, less $0.9M of other expense, net.
follow100Note: Rows may not add exactly due to rounding. Reddit lost $236.69 for every $100 of revenue this quarter — almost all of it the one-off stock-compensation charge triggered by the IPO, not cash out the door.

takeaways.title: First quarter as a public company
takeaways.text: Revenue grew 48% from a year ago to $243M in the quarter Reddit listed on the NYSE, with Daily Active Uniques up 37% to 82.7 million and Weekly Active Uniques up 40% to 306.2 million.

takeaways.title: One charge explains the loss
takeaways.text: When Reddit went public in March, years of employee restricted stock units vested at once, booking $595.5M of stock-based compensation and related payroll taxes across the cost lines. That single non-cash-heavy charge is why a fast-growing ad business still posted a $575M GAAP net loss.

takeaways.title: Adjusted EBITDA turned positive
takeaways.text: Adjusted EBITDA was $10.0M — Reddit's first positive first quarter on that basis, versus -$50.2M a year ago — and operating cash flow was $32.1M despite the GAAP loss, with gross margin at 88.6%.

footerNote: Figures are from Reddit's Q1 2024 earnings release (Exhibit 99.1) and Form 10-Q, which report in thousands. Stock-based compensation and related payroll taxes of $595.5M — most of it a one-time charge as restricted stock units vested at the March 2024 IPO — sit inside the research & development, sales & marketing and general & administrative lines, which is why those lines dwarf revenue this quarter.
